reasoning: Both sets are thorough, single-package plans that cover all three stages in the spec, architecture, contract and tests, and both use sound RL designs. A proves DQN on CartPole and PPO on Pendulum against Stable-Baselines3, bootstraps on truncation, uses a sign-flip permutation test with Holm correction and a 20% margin, and co-trains with an opponent pool plus cross-play. B uses DQN part-removal runs, REINFORCE vs PPO with clip and value-baseline removals, alternating frozen-copy co-evolution with cross-play, and a one-fish library check. A wins on pipeline clarity: small single-owner steps with clean entry sketches, a spine baseline of online one-step TD, and a layout that follows the step owners. B's PL-01 hides most of training inside one branching `run_episodes` step. A's main weakness is milestone quality. M1 never produces a 'does the agent beat its baselines' verdict, because that was carved into M4 to meet a task-count limit. That makes the build order M1→M4→M2→M3, against the IDs, and M2–M4 have no Exit criteria. B's milestones are better: M1 is a real vertical slice ending in the full Snake experiment, and every milestone has checkable Exit criteria. But B's M3 (one pipeline) is lopsided, and M4's dependence on M3 rather than M2 is debatable. B also carries more stale text (a struck AGENT-01, retired contract entries). Its split-task packets cite internal functions that were retired from the contract, and several statistical tests use an 'at most 1 of 20' tolerance that a correct 5% test fails about 26% of the time. Task packets are about equally buildable. A's are missing type definitions (EvalResult, DQNConfig); B's are missing TestResult, EpisodeRecord, the memory API and the Snake start rules. On balance A edges B on content (4.0 vs 3.9); structure ties at 4.0, giving 8.0 vs 7.9.

strengths: Each hand-written algorithm is proven on a standard easy task (CartPole, Pendulum) against Stable-Baselines3 before its results are trusted, with a normalized score and 'unverified' marking
Pipeline step tables are small, single-owner and readable; entry sketches follow directly from the tables; the DQN spine is a real online-TD baseline
Statistics are carefully specified (sign-flip permutation, Holm, 20% margin over the scripted baseline), and the TC-19 tolerance is justified correctly from the binomial tail
The tank World is designed as configurable body kinds, so predator-prey extends it (TANK-10) instead of copying it
The replay viewer is interactive (step back, 0.25x–8x speed, sight circle) and also exports animations
weaknesses: M1 ends without any 'agent beats baselines' verdict; the learning check and report were split into M4 to fit a task-count limit
Roadmap build order is M1→M4→M2→M3, against the IDs; M2–M4 have no Exit criteria
The todo and plan list M1-T24 between T21 and T22
EvalResult and CheckResult are used but never defined in the contract
Split-task packets (e.g. T13) omit needed settings contracts and have no golden-case oracle

strengths: M1 is a full vertical slice: train, removal runs, evaluate with a hypothesis test, replays, charts and a full Snake experiment task
Pedagogically strong part-removal design: DQN without memory or target copy, REINFORCE vs PPO without clip or value baseline, and an opponent pool for co-evolution
Every milestone has checkable Exit criteria, and the build order matches the milestone IDs
Very concrete spec numbers and golden cases with worked values (TC-26 returns, TC-41 observation vectors)
The game protocol is role-aware from M1, so later stages don't rework Snake
weaknesses: PL-01's `run_episodes` step bundles the co-evolution and single-learner loops into one branching step
Several statistical test tolerances ('at most 1 of 20') are mis-justified and fail by chance about 26% of the time
The library check is a lopsided one-pipeline milestone, and predator-prey depends on it rather than on the tank milestone
Stale text is kept: the struck-through AGENT-01, a Retired list in the contract, and replan notes
Internal step functions were retired from the contract, so split-mode testers lack the APIs they must test; TestResult and EpisodeRecord are undefined
DQN is never checked against a reference, only PPO
